luaeval.py.summary: Check Lua files for syntax errors and quarantine the broken ones.
details: Parses every ``.lua`` file below the current directory with tree-sitter, follows the whole node tree looking for error or missing nodes and moves the files that fail into an ``error`` folder next to them (existing names get a numeric suffix).

m4a2mp3.py.summary: Convert an ``.m4a`` audio file to MP3 with ffmpeg.
details: Transcodes the input with ``libmp3lame`` at 64 kbit/s (video streams dropped), writes ``<name>.mp3`` next to it and prints the input/output sizes and their ratio.

magickcv.py.summary: Run ImageMagick-style edit operations on images with Pillow and OpenCV.
details: Parses the classic command line (``-resize``, ``-crop``, ``-rotate``, ``-flip``/``-flop``, ``-blur``, ``-sharpen``, ``-modulate``, ``-grayscale``, ``-negate``, ``-sepia-tone``, ``-threshold``, ``-alpha``, ``-gravity``, ``-strip`` ...) and applies the operations to the input image(s), writing the result to the output path. ``-identify`` prints the image properties instead of editing.

make_dep_graph.py.summary: Dump the dependency graph of the installed distributions as JSON.
details: Reads the ``METADATA`` of every ``.dist-info`` directory in the first ``site-packages`` on ``sys.path``, collects the ``Requires-Dist`` entries (versions and markers stripped) and writes ``package_dependencies.json``.

man_doc.py.summary: Render man pages to HTML with ``mandoc``.
details: Finds the man pages below the current directory (sections 1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8 and the ``.3*``/``.n`` variants, gzipped or not), converts each one with ``mandoc -T html``, writes ``<name>.html`` and deletes the original. Files are processed in parallel.

markdowntopdf.py.summary: Convert Markdown files to PDF with WeasyPrint.
details: Renders the Markdown (tables, magic links, better emphasis, fenced code; extras and a JSON config are accepted), styles it with the given CSS (``.xz`` supported, default ``/sdcard/_static/css/markdown.css.xz``) and writes one PDF per input, in parallel.

marked.py.summary: A pure-Python port of the JavaScript ``marked`` Markdown parser.
details: Exposes the ``Marked`` class plus ``Renderer``, ``Tokenizer``, ``Lexer``, ``Parser`` and ``Token`` so Markdown can be rendered to HTML programmatically. The module-level ``marked`` object is ready to use: ``marked.parse(text)``.
marked.py.notes: Library module: import ``marked`` rather than running it; there is no command-line entry point.

maturer.py.summary: Build a Rust/maturin extension and repackage it as a wheel.
details: Runs ``cargo build --release``, computes the platform wheel tag (``cp3XX``/free-threaded, normalised for 32-bit ARM) and packs the shared library with the expected ``.dist-info`` metadata into ``<name>-<version>-<tag>.whl``.
maturer.py.notes: Run from the crate root; it needs ``Cargo.toml`` and a working cargo toolchain.

mchist.py.summary: Import the ``[cmdline]`` section of Midnight Commander's history into ``.bash_history``.
details: Reads ``~/.local/share/mc/history``, takes the command lines of the ``[cmdline]`` block, removes duplicates and appends them to ``~/.bash_history``.

merge_enfa.py.summary: Merge English→Persian translation files into one dictionary.
details: Reads the JSON translation files it finds, merges the mappings (first value wins) and writes the combined dictionary back to disk.

merge_faen.py.summary: Merge Persian↔English translation pairs and keep the untranslated words aside.
details: Pairs the input files, loads the existing translations, merges the new entries and appends the words that could not be matched to the failed list, logging progress with loguru and saving as it goes.

mergecss.py.summary: Merge all CSS files of the current directory into ``merged.css``.
details: Calls ``cleancss -O2`` with duplicate-rule removal over ``*.css`` and writes the combined, minified stylesheet to ``merged.css``.

mergedic.py.summary: Merge several dictionaries into one JSON file, detecting the translation direction.
details: Discovers the dictionary inputs, decides for each pair which side is English (a plain ASCII heuristic), normalises the values and writes a single merged mapping with unique file names when the target already exists.

meta_to_ipynb.py.summary: Turn a package ``METADATA`` file into a Jupyter notebook.
details: Parses the core metadata header, splits the remaining description into Markdown text and fenced code blocks and writes ``<package>.ipynb`` with a title cell followed by one Markdown or code cell per section.
